messages:
maria: quick q — trying to DRY up our helm values by using an _includes_ file via .Files.Get, but my envFrom secret refs disappear when I flip useExternalSecrets: true in values. anyone seen weird precedence here?

alex: can you paste the values.yaml and the template snippet where you render envFrom? small paste is fine.

maria: sure, here's the values layout (simplified):
```yaml
# values.yaml
useExternalSecrets: true
app:
  image: org/app:1.2.3
  envFrom: 
    - secretRef: 
        name: app-static-secrets
```
and template snippet in deployment.yaml:
```yaml
envFrom:
{{- if .Values.app.envFrom }}
{{ toYaml .Values.app.envFrom | indent 12 }}
{{- end }}
```
when useExternalSecrets=false the secretRef block renders fine. when true, we mount external secrets via an external-secrets controller and want to omit the secretRef, but my include file approach is not toggling as expected.

kevin: two quick checks: 1) is there a global override like .Values.global.envFrom you're not aware of? 2) are you using `.Files.Get` to load a YAML file that itself contains `envFrom:`? Helm's toYaml + indent combos sometimes double-serialize if you load raw files.

maria: i do have a _includes/envs.yaml with the shared block, like:
```yaml
# _includes/envs.yaml
app_envFrom: |
  - secretRef:
      name: app-static-secrets
```
and in values.yaml i reference it: `app.envFrom: | {{ .Files.Get "_includes/envs.yaml" | fromYaml | .app_envFrom }}` (that was my attempt)

emily: hmm that expression looks off — `.Files.Get` returns a string; then using `fromYaml` should give you a map, but the pipes and dot scoping can be tricky. also using literal `|` in values plus toYaml in template can produce extra quoting. i'd simplify: put the envFrom array directly in values.yaml (not as a string) or use tpl to render templates inside values.

alex: example: put `_includes/envs.yaml` as a YAML sequence, then in values.yaml: `app: { envFrom: {{ .Files.Get "_includes/envs.yaml" | indent 2 }}}` — but that's not valid in plain values since values are loaded before templates. instead do this pattern in the template: `{{- $includes := .Files.Get "_includes/envs.yaml" | fromYaml }}
{{- if or (not .Values.useExternalSecrets) $includes.app_envFrom }}
envFrom:
{{ toYaml $includes.app_envFrom | indent 12 }}
{{- end }}`

maria: ok — so move the conditional into the template and parse the include file there, not try to pre-evaluate into values.yaml. that makes sense. any gotchas with `fromYaml` returning a list vs map? i had a panic in helm template locally once.

kevin: fromYaml preserves type. if your include contains a top-level sequence (like `- secretRef:`) then `fromYaml` returns a list and you can directly `toYaml` it. the panic usually comes from trying to index into a nil (e.g., `$includes.app_envFrom` when file is empty). guard with `with` or checks.

maria: thanks — i'll try this pattern:
```gotemplate
{{- $incs := .Files.Get "_includes/envs.yaml" | default "{}" | fromYaml }}
{{- if and (not .Values.useExternalSecrets) (hasKey $incs "app_envFrom") }}
envFrom:
{{ toYaml ($incs.app_envFrom) | indent 12 }}
{{- end }}
```
and make `_includes/envs.yaml` be:
```yaml
app_envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: app-static-secrets
```
will report back after I test.

kevin: nice, also add a unit test for the template rendering with both true/false for useExternalSecrets. caught one of these for svc-account mounting last week.

maria: got it. thx all! will follow up if oddness persists. :pray:
